excerpts: Taiwan Company Formation and Compliance for Foreign Investors Taiwan company formation and compliance is our service for foreign individuals and foreign companies setting up a subsidiary, branch or new company in Taiwan. We handle the investment application to the Department of Investment Review, company registration, work permits and residence for foreign managers, then ongoing contracts, governance and tax compliance once the business is running. By **Queenie Wu** , Attorney at Law (New York State Bar) · Attorney of Foreign Legal Affairs in Taiwan · WU LAW INTL PLLC, Taipei · Updated October 27, 2026 Taiwan Company Formation and Compliance for Foreign Investors Can a foreigner own 100% of a Taiwan company? Yes, in most industries. Under Article 7 of the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Taiwan publishes a Negative List of prohibited and restricted industries. Only restricted industries carry shareholding caps set by the competent authority; in every other industry a foreign investor may hold 100%. Taiwan's Company Act no longer sets a general minimum capital, and the Department of Investment Review states there is no minimum investment amount, though licensed industries may set their own. (Source: [Invest Taiwan FAQ](https://investtaiwan.nat.gov.tw/faqQContent?lang=cht&search=5) ) How long does Taiwan company formation take? Four steps: reserve the company name, file the investment application with the Department of Investment Review (Form A), remit the capital and have the amount verified (Form C), then register the company with the approval letters. Invest Taiwan lists the Department's review time as 2 to 4 days for non-restricted cases at or under NT$500 million, and 10 to 30 days for restricted, large or M&A cases. Add time for document authentication abroad, bank remittance and company registration; the total depends on your case. (Source: [Invest Taiwan FAQ](https://investtaiwan.nat.gov.tw/faqQContent?lang=cht&search=4) ) What capital is needed for a founder work permit? The Ministry of Labor sets the threshold on the employer, not the person. For a foreign-invested company less than one year old, paid-in capital or Taiwan operating funds of NT$500,000 or more qualifies (alternatives include NT$3 million in revenue). After the first year, the test becomes average Taiwan revenue of NT$3 million or more over the latest one or three years. The foreign national must also qualify, for example as the manager of a company in which foreign investors hold more than one third of the shares.
